recent_posts.title: Introducing AMD DGF SuperCompression
recent_posts.summary: AMD has released DGF SuperCompression (DGFS) as part of the AMD DGF SDK v1.2 update. DGFS is a software compression layer on top of the Dense Geometry Format (DGF) that reduces storage size by up to 22% compared to raw DGF blocks, and roughly 20% when both are GDeflate-compressed. Unlike raw DGF blocks, DGFS is not directly consumable by hardware but can be decoded to either DGF blocks or conventional vertex/index buffers (meshlets), enabling a single asset format to target both DGF and non-DGF devices. The system uses cluster-granular compression with techniques including vertex de-duplication, delta encoding, zig-zag encoding, and byte interleaving. Decode performance on a single CPU core is fast enough for streaming scenarios, and a GPU-based decoder is also viable.

recent_posts.title: AMD DGF: An Open Geometry Compression Standard
recent_posts.summary: AMD is announcing a partnership with Samsung to develop a multivendor Vulkan extension for Dense Geometry Format (DGF), a block-based geometry compression standard. DGF addresses the growing mismatch between high-complexity geometry (as seen in systems like Nanite) and current ray tracing APIs, which require decoding compressed formats into uncompressed acceleration structures — increasing memory pressure and build latency. By moving geometry compression into a standardized, hardware-native format, DGF aims to do for geometry what DXT/ETC/ASTC did for textures. AMD is also releasing an updated DGF SDK with a preview of DGF SuperCompression, which further reduces size and simplifies rendering on non-DGF hardware.

recent_posts.title: Introducing MiniDXNN: MLP library for DirectX 12
recent_posts.summary: AMD has released MiniDXNN, an open-source MLP inference library built natively for HLSL and DirectX 12. It targets game developers and graphics programmers who want to integrate small neural networks (e.g., neural radiance caching, neural texture compression) into DX12 rendering pipelines without compute API interop overhead. The library leverages AMD Radeon RX 9000 series matrix cores via cooperative vector APIs, delivering performance comparable to dedicated ML frameworks. This initial release includes optimized MLP inference kernels, unit tests, sample applications, full source code, and documentation. Training support is planned for a future release. Cooperative vector support currently requires AMD developer drivers and RX 9000 series hardware.

recent_posts.title: Introducing MinDXNN: MLP library for DirectX 12
recent_posts.summary: AMD has released MinDXNN, a native HLSL and DirectX 12 library for multi-layer perceptron (MLP) inference. It leverages AMD Radeon RX 9000 series GPU matrix cores via cooperative vector APIs, delivering performance comparable to dedicated ML frameworks without requiring compute API interop (e.g., HIP). The initial release includes optimized MLP inference kernels, unit tests, sample applications for 2D image reconstruction, and full source code. Training support is planned for the next release. Currently requires AMD developer drivers and RX 9000 series hardware.

recent_posts.title: Welcome to the AMD FSR SDK 2.2, now available on GPUOpen
recent_posts.summary: AMD has released FSR SDK 2.2, the first major update since the December 2025 FSR 'Redstone' launch. The update delivers two key improvements: FSR Upscaling 4.1 with enhanced image quality especially in motion, improved ultra-performance and dynamic resolution scaling modes; and FSR Ray Regeneration 1.1 with quality and memory improvements plus debug view modes. Both ML-powered features require AMD RDNA 4 architecture GPUs (Radeon RX 9000 Series), while analytical fallback modes (FSR 3) remain available for older hardware. The SDK supports a single implementation across handhelds, consoles, and PCs. Binaries and limited source are available on GitHub.

recent_posts.title: Enhancing DirectX Testing with AMD Smoldr
recent_posts.summary: AMD has released Smoldr, an open-source command-line tool that lets developers run DirectX 12 HLSL shaders using simple text scripts — no C++ required. Similar to Google's Amber for Vulkan, Smoldr handles shader compilation via DXIL, pipeline creation, resource management, and compute or raytracing dispatches. It supports the Microsoft Agility SDK for experimental HLSL features and integrates with AMD Radeon GPU Profiler. The tool is work-in-progress with plans to add mesh shader support next.

recent_posts.title: AMD and Microsoft partner on DirectX ML, DirectStorage, and developer tools at GDC 2026
recent_posts.summary: AMD and Microsoft announced several collaborative developer technologies at GDC 2026. Key highlights include DirectStorage 1.4 with Zstandard compression support for faster game asset streaming, new PIX tooling features (DirectX Dump Files, Live Shader Debugging preview, Shader Explorer), and major DirectX ML advancements including DX Linear Algebra for matrix-matrix operations in HLSL and the DirectX Compute Graph Compiler for model-level GPU acceleration. Advanced Shader Delivery addresses shader compilation stutter on PC, and the Agility SDK 1.619 officially releases Shader Model 6.9 with DXR 1.2 SER support. AMD is providing driver support for these features, with most tooling updates arriving Q2 2026.

recent_posts.title: Driving the future: frictionless automotive HMI development with Epic Games & AMD Ryzen AI Embedded P100 series
recent_posts.summary: At CES 2026, Epic Games and AMD demonstrated the Unreal Engine 5 Next-Gen HMI Experience running on AMD Ryzen AI Embedded P100 Series processors. The showcase unifies instrument clusters, maps, navigation, and third-party apps into a single UE5 instance delivering 60 FPS across multiple displays. Key technical innovations include the Android Single Instance Service (ASIS) for hosting one engine instance as a shared service, and MultiWorld support for rendering distinct camera views simultaneously within the same scene. AMD RDNA 3.5 graphics enable gaming-class visuals in the cockpit, while a Xen-based virtualization framework isolates OS domains for safety. The platform bridges IVI and ADAS, supports functional safety partitioning, and gives developers tools like Unreal Insights for profiling the full HMI on real hardware.

recent_posts.title: HIP Threads: GPU power for teams without GPU experts
recent_posts.summary: HIP Threads is a new C++ concurrency library from AMD that lets development teams offload CPU hotspots to AMD GPUs without requiring GPU expertise or kernel rewrites. By mapping familiar C++ threading patterns directly to GPU execution, teams can incrementally port performance-critical code and see speedups in days rather than months. Early benchmarks on AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 hardware show significant gains on workloads like SAXPY, ray tracing, and sparse matrix multiplication compared to standard CPU threading.

recent_posts.title: new multithreading dev log & full AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO breakdown
recent_posts.summary: Youthcat Games rebuilt Dyson Sphere Program's multithreading system from scratch, achieving an 88% performance improvement in logic frame efficiency. The new system introduces custom core binding, dynamic task allocation with work-stealing, flexible task scheduling that allows parallel execution of previously sequential logic, and enhanced thread synchronization using hybrid spinlocks. Testing on AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 9985WX (64 cores, 128 threads) revealed scheduling overhead and false sharing issues at extreme thread counts, which were subsequently optimized to double frame rates on the same save file.

top_posts.title: Introducing AMD GI-1.2 with multibounce indirect real-time rendering
top_posts.summary: AMD released GI-1.2, an enhanced real-time Global Illumination solution that introduces multibounce rendering to capture additional light bounces through a two-level hash grid cache system. The update addresses the previous version's limitation where scenes appeared darker than path-traced references by extending ray paths from first-bounce cells to create second-bounce cells, significantly improving reflections and overall lighting accuracy. GI-1.2 is available in AMD Capsaicin Framework v1.3, which also adds HDR display support, DPI awareness, and AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution integration including FSR 4 for RDNA 4 GPUs.

top_posts.title: A beginner's guide to deploying LLMs with AMD on Windows using PyTorch
top_posts.summary: A comprehensive beginner's tutorial for setting up and running Large Language Models locally on Windows PCs using AMD GPUs or APUs with PyTorch. Covers installation of PyTorch with ROCm support, creating virtual environments, running the Llama 3.2 1B model, and building an interactive chatbot. Includes step-by-step instructions for developers new to AI frameworks, requiring only Python knowledge and compatible AMD hardware from RX 7000/9000 series or Ryzen AI 300/Max APUs.

top_posts.title: Announcing AMD Schola v2: Next-generation reinforcement learning for Unreal Engine
top_posts.summary: AMD Schola v2 is an open-source reinforcement learning plugin for Unreal Engine 5 that enables training and deploying AI agents. The major update introduces a flexible inference architecture with modular agent/policy/stepper components, native Minari dataset support for offline RL, dynamic agent spawning and deletion during episodes, an enhanced command-line interface, improved Blueprint integration, and updated support for Gymnasium 1.1+, Ray RLlib, and Stable-Baselines3 2.x. The plugin bridges Unreal Engine with Python-based RL frameworks, supporting use cases from game NPC training to robotic simulations.

top_posts.title: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 4 plugin updated for Unreal Engine 5.7
top_posts.summary: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 4 plugin now supports Unreal Engine 5.7, offering improved temporal stability, detail preservation, and reduced ghosting for AMD RDNA 4 graphics cards. The update includes automatic driver-based FSR version updates, fallback to FSR 3.1.5 for older AMD GPUs, and analytical frame generation for Radeon RX 5000 series and newer. The plugin integrates with AMD Radeon Anti-Lag 2 for additional latency reduction and prepares games for the upcoming FSR Redstone ML frame generation feature.

top_posts.title: Animating geometry with AMD DGF
top_posts.summary: AMD's Dense Geometry Format (DGF) SDK now supports animation-aware encoding, allowing developers to animate compressed triangle meshes efficiently. The new pipeline overwrites vertex positions in DGF blocks each frame while maintaining stable topology, achieving animation updates for 252K triangle scenes in just 20 microseconds. The approach uses linear vertex blending, quantization compute shaders, and careful bit-width management to preserve DGF's compression benefits while enabling real-time geometry animation for ray tracing applications.
